This arbitrage scam inflates healthcare costs across the board, with employers losing $5B annually in rebates and states hemorrhaging $1B+ to price-gouging. Reform isn’t optional—it’s survival.

Kill the middlemen, enforce price transparency, and redirect savings to patients, not hospital execs’ pockets.

The Nancy Gardner Sewell Medicare Multi-Cancer Early Detection Screening Coverage Act (H.R. 842) sounds noble—until you follow the money. Early detection saves lives, but Medicare’s track record shows every dollar allocated gets vacuumed into bureaucratic overhead and Big Pharma’s pricing schemes. Case in point: The same bill allocates funds for “evidence-based coverage parameters” that’ll let CMS bureaucrats dictate terms, not doctors.

Meanwhile, China’s racing ahead in MCED tech while D.C. drowns in red tape. Real reform? Audit Medicare’s $1 trillion cancer spending over the next decade and redirect savings to patients, not middlemen.

Innovation shouldn’t mean blank checks for the same failed system.
